geographical_area: Romagna (Ravenna, Forlì-Cesena, Rimini provinces and neighbouring areas). The profile writes a Ravenna–Forlì koiné, because the usable open sources (Ercolani 1960, Ravenna countryside; Wikipedia grammar sections) favour it; Rimini differences are flagged where documented. The proposed Rimini reference is therefore not adopted as a base norm.
orthographic_conventions: Vitali-style modern Romagnol: diacritics for vowel quality/length (é è ê ë ó ò ô ö ã), apostrophe for clitics and truncations (t', n', l'è, j'è), apocopated infinitives (magnè, fé', durmì), e' for the masculine article, no doubled consonants (pataca), voiced z written z. Ercolani's older spelling and Rimini variants are accepted as alternatives.
description_en: Romagnol of Romagna: obligatory subject clitics (a, t', e'/u, la, i, al), preverbal negation n', masculine article e', metaphonic masculine plurals (can/chèn), a rich vowel system with length and nasal vowels, four conjugations and impersonal u s' constructions, plus a teasing, ironic register. The word pataca means 'fool, harmless show-off'.
description_it: Romagnolo di Romagna: clitici soggetto obbligatori (a, t', e'/u, la, i, al), negazione preverbale n', articolo maschile e', plurali maschili metafonetici (can/chèn), sistema vocalico ricco con lunghezza e vocali nasali, quattro coniugazioni e costruzioni impersonali con u s', e un registro canzonatorio e ironico. La parola pataca significa 'sciocco, sbruffone innocuo'.

identifier_word.meaning_en: Romagnol: fool, simpleton, harmless show-off (also vulgar term for female genitalia).
identifier_word.meaning_it: Romagnolo: sciocco, minchione, sbruffone ingenuo e innocuo (anche termine volgare per la vulva).
identifier_word.attestation: Ercolani's Vocabolario romagnolo-italiano (1960) has 'patacca, sm. agg., minchione, sciocco', pl. patéca, and notes the genital sense under spatachéss. Popular FAQ pages describe the harmless-braggart nuance. Standard Italian 'patacca' (junk coin) is a different sense. The mode name is the common Romagnol form with single c; Ercolani spells it with cc. The catalog gloss 'originally vulgar' is only partly true: the vulgar sense exists but the main attested sense is 'fool'.

known_limitations: No native-speaker review: all example sentences are AI-illustrative.

Reference norm is a Ravenna–Forlì koiné, not Rimini as the brief proposed; Rimini paradigms (essere a sèm, magnè) are only partly documented, and the printed Rimini 2sg of essere ('t'cè') is uncertain.
The main lexical source (Ercolani 1960) is Ravenna-countryside, OCR text with noisy diacritics (voiced z rendered § ? ^); forms were normalised and must not be treated as precise spelling.
Documented verb coverage is partial: fare and andare lack a full present paradigm (only a vèg and infinitives are attested), so examples avoid them and use impersonal u s' constructions.
Examples use words outside the lexicon (e.g. ucupèda, pulida, cliént) built regularly; they are low confidence.
Only one blasphemy (smadunèr) is documented, as a verb with no verbatim formula, so no oath text is generated; level-5 vulgarity is built from level 3-4 items.
The catalog describes the identifier as 'originally vulgar'; sources support 'fool' as the main sense with a separate vulgar genital sense.
Three proverbs (Chi sèmna vènt..., Us impèra..., Savè zcòr...) come only from a low-reliability web list and are marked unverified.
The Bolognese mode (socmel) is written in parallel; contrast statements in profile section 14 should be checked against it once available.
